::: {#thm-double-inclusion}
#### Equal sets are subsets of each other

Let $A$ and $B$ be sets.
Then $A = B$ if and only if $A \subseteq B$ and $B \subseteq A$.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

By @def-set, $A = B$ means that every $x$ has $x \in A \Leftrightarrow x \in B$.
By @thm-biconditional-split, that biconditional is the same as
"$x \in A \Rightarrow x \in B$, and $x \in B \Rightarrow x \in A$".
A conjunction is true for every $x$ exactly when each of its two parts is true for every $x$.
The first conditional, for every $x$, is $A \subseteq B$ (@def-subset),
and the second, for every $x$, is $B \subseteq A$.

:::

:::
